post.description:
Exchange a valid refresh token for a fresh access token (and a rotated
refresh token). The submitted refresh token's `sid` MUST match the user's
`active_session_id` — otherwise the session has been revoked (because the
user logged in from another device or explicitly logged out) and we
respond 401 detail=session_revoked so the FE can clean its local state.

Refresh-token rotation: every successful call mints a brand-new refresh
token AND assigns the user a brand-new `active_session_id`. This means an
attacker who steals a refresh token can only use it once — on next legit
use, the real user's session will already have been rotated and the
attacker's call returns session_revoked.

Full money-flow breakdown — categorizes every successful transaction

  • UTR direct-added deposits
  • Service margin (platform fees on bookings)
  • Shop margin (platform fees on orders)

Outflow categories (cash leaving / being redistributed):
  • Referral commissions credited to user wallets (net of GST)
  • GST collected (regulatory hold)
  • User withdrawals (completed)
  • Cascade overflow rerouted to admin

post.description:
One-shot cleanup for the buggy cancel-refund flow that pre-dated the
proper double-entry handling.

Symptoms it fixes:
  • COD orders were credited admin's shop_commission AT PLACEMENT
    (before cash was collected). When cancelled, the bogus refund
    was deposited into the user's wallet too, doubling the drift.
  • Wallet orders never reversed admin's commission on cancel.

Strategy (idempotent — flagged via order.legacy_drift_cleaned):
  1. For every cancelled order without a *_reversal txn:
       a) reverse the admin's `shop_commission` bucket
       b) reverse any vendor_sale credits
       c) for COD-paid orders: the user got a phantom refund (no real
          money flowed in or out) — debit the user's wallet back IF
          they still have at least that much balance. Otherwise log a
          `legacy_drift_residual` audit note (manual admin write-off).

Dec 2026 — Lazy-load endpoint for base64 product images with
ON-THE-FLY THUMBNAILING + aggressive caching.

Query params:
  * `w`  — target width in px.  When set (e.g. `w=360` for grid cards),
           we resize the source image, re-encode as JPEG at quality
           `q` (default 72) → typical 200 KB source → 25-40 KB thumb.
           For the customer shop grid this is a **~90% payload
           reduction on top of the base64 → binary conversion**.
  * `q`  — JPEG quality 40-95, default 72.  Bigger for detail page.
  * Omit `w` → returns the original (used by product detail).

Caching:
  * ETag = sha1(image bytes)[:16] — client sends `If-None-Match`
    and the server returns 304 Not Modified when unchanged (0 KB
    response body).
  * `Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800, immutable` — client /
    CDN caches the exact w×q variant for a full week.

    net_worth =
          bank_balance
        + cash_on_hand
        + receivables (pending payments + cashback owed by sellers)
        − user_liability
        − vendor_payable
        − pending_withdrawals
        − gst_payable

migration is required.

no wallet was touched, so "adjustment money" was a number on a screen
that no refund and no cashback could ever spend, while still shifting the
reconciliation display. It now posts through the real ledger
(`shop_money.credit` / `shop_money.debit`), so the balance it claims to

The phone tells us why it could NOT register.

Without this, a device that never obtains an FCM token (notification
permission refused, a Dual-App / cloned instance with no Play Services
binding, an emulator, a Firebase init failure) is indistinguishable from
a server that never sent — both just look like "no device registered".
Recorded against the account so Admin → Push diagnostics can name the
real blocker instead of guessing.

Super admin smoke test — sends a push and returns the FULL evidence:
the relay HTTP status, the relay's response body, whether the relay key
is injected, and the target device's registration record. This is the
proof that separates "server didn't send" from "Firebase rejected" from
"this phone never registered".

get.description:
The whole pipeline in one response: relay key state, device
registrations, and the last N send attempts with the exact upstream
status and body. Nothing here is inferred — every field is what the
relay actually answered.
One account's push truth: its devices and its last 50 attempts.

post.description:
Create + deliver a broadcast to every user in the chosen audience.

Delivery steps per user:
  1. Find / create an announcement thread between admin and user.
  2. Insert a chat_messages doc tagged `is_broadcast=true`.
  3. Bump the thread's last_message_at so it surfaces at the top of
     the user's chat list.

Push notifications are sent in chunks of 100 (Emergent relay hard cap).

Copy legacy `users.status` -> `users.approval_status` where missing.

Older registration flows wrote the bare `status` field; newer code
(and every admin query that segments the audience for broadcasts /
payouts) reads `approval_status`. Running this once normalises both
fields so future queries can rely on `approval_status` alone.

get.description:
One page of the vendor's catalogue, images included.

`limit` is capped at 25 because each product can carry several base64
photos — the client keeps calling with a bumped `offset` until
`has_more` is false and writes ONE file at the end.

post.description:
Restore a page of products into the CALLING vendor's account.

Body:
  products   : list of product objects from an export file (required)
  mode       : "merge" (default) | "replace"
  first_chunk: true on the first call — only then does "replace" wipe the
               vendor's existing products, so a multi-chunk restore
               doesn't delete what the previous chunk just inserted.
  restore_session: an id the client keeps for the whole file. Every row
               this restore creates or updates is stamped with it, and
               stamped rows are never matched again — otherwise a file
               listing the same product name in two different chunks had
               its second chunk overwrite the row the first chunk had just
               created, silently losing a product.

get.description:
What's in the database right now — the client uses this to plan the
download and to show the admin a preview before anything happens.

One page of one collection. `limit` is deliberately client-tunable so
the app can drop to 25 for image-heavy collections like `products`.
Everything the app holds about ONE account (customer or vendor).
The whole app as ONE streamed .json download.
Everything about ONE account (customer or shop) as one streamed .json.

post.description:
Start packing a backup file on the server. Returns a job id the app
polls; the finished file downloads in seconds. Works even if the app is
closed while packing.

get.description:
Stream the finished file from its Mongo chunks — fast, because the
packing already happened.

post.description:
Replay one page of one collection from a backup file.

Body:
  collection : target collection name (required)
  docs       : list of documents (required)
  mode       : "merge" (upsert by id) | "wipe" (delete the collection's
               rows on the first chunk, then insert)
  first_chunk: true on the first page for this collection
  danger_pin : the 6-digit Danger PIN — same gate as Danger Zone

Money is restored exactly as it appears in the file (owner's choice); this
is a data replay, so no commission, payout or notification logic runs.

get.description: The vendor's live zone, exactly as the customer filter reads it.
"Do I deliver to 517641?" — same answer the customer's shop gets.
How many shops can deliver to the place the customer just picked.

post.description: Set a new password (given or generated) and show it once.
Sign one listed device out (its session id is pulled from the account).
Keep this device signed in, sign every other one out.

Jun-2026 — pay for a plan straight from the Slangcart wallet.

No gateway, so there is no bank row: the money is already ours. The
wallet debit is atomic (guarded on the balance) so a double tap cannot
book two recharges, and the booking itself goes through the SAME
`book_recharge_order` the online path uses — same order, same seller
credit, same ledger rows.

Oct-2026 — pay-online for a recharge plan.

A recharge is not a shop order: nothing ships, there is no cart and no
delivery charge, so it gets its own attempt row and its own verify step.
The money path is identical to the shop flow (same Razorpay creds, same
signature + amount verification, same mock-mode behaviour in preview),
which is exactly why it reuses these helpers instead of inventing a
second payment pipeline.

Confirm the Razorpay payment and book the recharge.

Idempotent: a repeated call on an already-paid attempt returns the same
recharge instead of charging or booking twice.

get.description:
Past recharges, newest first, each one ready to REPEAT.

Jun-2026 — the row carries everything the pay flow needs (plan id, kind,
circle, operator, the number) plus whether the plan is still live and at
what price, so "Repeat" is one tap and never sends the shopper to a plan
that has since been pulled or re-priced.

A paid-but-not-yet-placed attempt, so the app can resume instead of
asking the customer to pay a second time.

Application + approval state. Safe to call for ANY logged-in user, so
the profile screen can decide what to show without guessing.

Which sellers this rider delivers for, plus every seller to choose from.

Oct 2026 — the projection used to mix inclusion with `"dp_pincodes": 0`,
which MongoDB rejects, so this endpoint always 500'd and the admin saw
"could not load shops". Every seller is now returned with the pincodes
they serve so the admin can filter the list PIN-wise before selecting.

put.description:
Replace the rider's seller mapping. Rows are deactivated rather than
deleted so historical orders keep their audit trail.

get.description:
The seller's panel calls this to know whether order movement is his job.

When a rider is mapped to the shop, the SELLER only accepts (confirms) or
cancels an order — every delivery stage after that belongs to the rider.
The shops this rider delivers for, with live order counts.
Orders from the rider's MAPPED sellers only. Nothing else is visible.

patch.description:
Advance an order. Delegates to the SAME status engine the vendor and
admin use, so delivery money (vendor credit, delivery fee, cashback)
moves exactly once and exactly the same way whoever taps the button.

On `delivered` with cash due, the COD cash is recorded into the rider's
cash-in-hand as a liability to Slangcart — he has our money until he
remits it. He is never credited a delivery fee: riders earn nothing here.

get.description:
Open orders grouped by CUSTOMER, across every shop mapped to me.

Jun-2026 — pass the rider's own `lat`/`lng` and every doorstep comes back
with `distance_km`, nearest first, so he rides one loop instead of
criss-crossing the town. Falls back to the pincode centroid when an
address has no coordinates, and to the old most-orders-first order when
the rider hasn't shared his location.

post.description:
Move EVERY open order of one customer (from my mapped shops).

`status` empty  → each order steps to its own next stage.
`status` given  → every order jumps straight to that stage
                  (the rider's "Mark all delivered").
Orders already at or past the target are skipped, never re-posted, so
the cash ledger can't double-count.

get.description: Wallet and net worth come from the SAME view, so they can never drift.

Oct 2026 — the rider's EARNINGS ledger (personal wallet only).

Delivery commissions in, withdrawals out. COD cash never appears here:
that pot is Slangcart's money and lives in /me/cash-transactions.
Where the money came from, what is still owed, and per-shop split.
Every cash-collected / cash-paid row, newest first.

post.description: Open a Razorpay checkout for the cash the rider is paying in.

Money received. ONE movement, three consistent records:

1. the rider's cash-in-hand is debited (he no longer holds our money)
2. a Group 7 BANK CREDIT is written, so bank ledger == bank statement
3. the matching orders are marked remitted and the vendor-wise split is
   recorded, so Group 2 liability is released against the right sellers

Jun-2026 owner request — settle Slangcart's cash from the rider's OWN
wallet balance, so "Cash to pay" is always `cash in hand − what his
wallet can cover`.

This is a pure SET-OFF, not a payment: we owed the rider his wallet
balance, he owed us the COD cash, so both sides shrink by the same
rupee. Deliberately NO bank_ledger row — nothing arrives in the bank, and
writing one would double-count the money in the Treasury. The admin's
net worth is untouched: an asset (cash on hand) and a liability (rider
wallet) both fall by `amount`.

get.description: Everything the rider has: summary, cash ledger, deliveries, payments.
What the paywall, the upsell banner and every locked card read.
Every shop with its effective cashback % and delivery charge.
